scenario.description: A chief legal officer must approve the company's Form S-8 filing package for its 2026 equity incentive plan, including the registered share amount, participant tax treatment, and resale disclosure materials, with input from corporate governance, tax, and securities counsel.

shared_context.S1: The company plans to file a Form S-8 next Tuesday for its 2026 equity incentive plan.
shared_context.S2: The board has approved the equity incentive plan, and the filing package is being prepared for signature.
shared_context.S3: The plan will cover employee and consultant awards, including awards to senior executives.
shared_context.S4: As part of the firm's standard pre-filing review, Elena asks corporate governance, tax, and securities counsel to identify any required corrections or supporting materials before she approves the filing.

PF1.text: Martin checked the executed board resolutions and confirmed that they authorize registration of exactly 860000 shares under the 2026 plan, not the 1000000 shares currently shown in the draft; he has not yet updated the filing checklist.

PF2.text: Nisha reviewed the final plan text and confirmed that incentive stock options may be granted only to employees, while consultant awards must be designated as nonqualified stock options; this tax classification has not yet been reflected in the filing summary.

PF3.text: Caleb reviewed the award schedule and confirmed that the chief executive's planned resale of plan shares requires a reoffer prospectus to accompany the Form S-8 package because the chief executive is an affiliate; the draft package does not include one.

acceptance_conditions: The filing must register exactly 860000 shares authorized by the board resolutions.
The filing summary must state that incentive stock options are available only to employees.
Consultant awards must be designated as nonqualified stock options.
The Form S-8 package must include a reoffer prospectus for the chief executive's resale.
The filing checklist must include a correction commitment addressing the share count and matching it to the executed board resolutions.

content_checks.C3: decisions['consultant_award_type'] in ['nonqualified stock options', 'NSO', 'non-qualified stock options']
content_checks.C5: any(c['type'] == 'correction' and (c['target'] == 'Martin Shaw' or c['target'] == 'filing team') for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The draft lists 1000000 shares, but PF1 changes the filing to exactly 860000 shares and requires a correction commitment tied to the executed board resolutions.
The general plan coverage does not establish tax classification; PF2 changes ISO eligibility to employees only and changes consultant awards to nonqualified stock options.
The ordinary filing package has no resale disclosure requirement visible in the shared record, while PF3 changes it to require a reoffer prospectus for the affiliate chief executive's resale.
